title: Graceful node quarantine and reconcile sagas for private VPC health failures
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Design and implement an automated, auditable quarantine + reconcile flow for Private (VPC) nodes that fail health checks intermittently or enter degraded states during upgrades. The goal is to minimize customer-visible impact by cordoning affected capacity, snapshotting ephemeral state (KV cache), attempting safe repairs, and replacing nodes when repair attempts fail. This ticket produces the runbook, Terraform guard modules, orchestration sagas, and a small automation service to execute idempotent heals.
runbook_summary: When a Private node fails liveness or probe checks repeatedly within a short window, trigger node quarantine: shift traffic away, snapshot in-memory KV state to S3-compatible store, run a series of automated repairs (iptables reset, kernel module reload, attach/detach ENI), and if repairs do not converge after two attempts, mark node for replacement and let Terraform create a fresh node. All steps must be safe-apply guarded and reversible where possible.
remediation_steps: 1) Detection: Alert fires from probe-monitor with signature 'vpc-node-flap-5x-2m' and low-traffic-sla flag
2) Quarantine: QuarantineController sets node label 'quarantined=true' and adds to routing blacklist to divert requests to dedicated fallback pool
3) Snapshot: Trigger KV cache checkpoint procedure: flush prefix cache, create atomic snapshot to internal S3 with metadata and sequence number
4) Preflight Terraform: Run 'terraform plan' using the drift-detector module; fail if plan contains destructive ops without manual approval
5) Automated repair (attempt 1): Run repair script sequence (iptables reset, restart inference service, reattach ENI if detached), then wait 45s and run liveness probe
6) Automated repair (attempt 2): If still failing, run kernel module reload, NVMe remap, and re-sync network routes; re-run health probes
7) Replace node: If both repairs fail, use Terraform 'create replacement' flow: taint node, let autoscaler allocate new instance, and move traffic after readiness
8) Rewarm: On replacement node, rehydrate KV cache from snapshot and validate token-level cache checksums
9) Postmortem markers: Append incident tags to node metadata and push reconciliation summary to incident-tracker and Confluence template
automation_design: A small orchestration microservice (QuarantineController) will coordinate steps and call existing infra primitives. It will use idempotent APIs: snapshot/create/restore, terraform-dryrun, and node-state transitions. The reconcile saga runs in our workflow engine (ReconcileSaga) with compensating transactions and timeouts. All Terraform applies must run through the 'safe-apply' gate that enforces plan review for non-noop changes and requires OOB approve for destructive changes in production private accounts.
reconciliation_saga_flow: event: probe-failed -> look up node health history
if flap_count >= threshold -> mark for quarantine
snapshot KV cache -> run preflight checks
execute repair sequence 1 -> wait -> run probes
if still failing -> execute repair sequence 2 -> wait -> run probes
if still failing -> trigger terraform replacement AND notify oncall with Slack + phone
post-replacement -> rehydrate caches -> validation -> remove quarantine label
verification_checks: cache checksum matches snapshot metadata within 5s of completion
traffic ramping obeys circuit-breaker thresholds (10% step-ups)
terraform plan reports no unintended destructive changes
rollback_and_safety: All Terraform applies for replacement run in a staging workspace first with identical module versions
Safe-apply gate prevents simultaneous replacement of >20% of a private pool
QuarantineController supports manual abort and rollback and will unquarantine if snapshot restore fails
Alert and require human approval for any operation touching customer-managed network ACLs or security groups
